title: Organizing Principles for Moiré Quantum Matter
authors: Qiaoling Xu, Yifan Gao, Tao Zhang, Ammon Fischer, Yi Jiang, Hanqi Pi, Zike Fan, Dongdong An, Kun Zhou, Yingjian Li, Yongqing Li, Yuhao Fu, Lei Wang, Lijun Zhang, B. Andrei Bernevig, Dante M. Kennes, Enge Wang, Angel Rubio, Lede Xian
abstract: Moiré flat bands in van der Waals bilayers are usually discussed through a small set of mechanisms associated with the $Γ$ and $K$ valleys of hexagonal crystals, and more recently with $M$-valleys systems. Here we show that this view is incomplete. The momentum-space location and effective local orbital character of the monolayer's band edge, in conjunction with the moiré symmetry and the symmetry representations of the resulting bands, provide a general set of organizing variables for the emergent low-energy moiré Hamiltonian. Applying fully relaxed first-principles calculations, band unfolding and symmetry-representation analysis to more than 600 commensurate twisted bilayers spanning all 2D lattice classes, we identify several routes to moiré quantum matter beyond the conventional single-orbital paradigm. The resulting flat bands realize trigonal, honeycomb, square, checkerboard and kagome-like Hubbard models with single-orbital, multi-orbital and multi-site Hilbert spaces; spin-orbit-coupled multi-orbital flat bands exhibit symmetry-indicated topology beyond the conventional $K$-valley setting; and nonsymmorphic moiré symmetries enforce semimetallic flat-band connectivity. Analogous quasi-one-dimensional flat-band structures are found in $M$-valley hexagonal systems and $X$-valley square or rectangular systems resulting from emergent momentum-space nonsymmorphic symmetries. Separately, coupled multi-valley manifolds with kagome-like connectivity are identified in several systems whose parent band edges lie at non-high-symmetry points. These results establish a valley-orbital-symmetry framework for connecting parent-material electronic structure to emergent moiré Hamiltonians relevant to correlated, topological and symmetry-enforced moiré phases.
summary: This paper introduces a general, symmetry-based framework to classify emergent moiré Hamiltonians in twisted van der Waals heterostructures. By analyzing hundreds of bilayers using first-principles calculations, the authors move beyond simple single-orbital models. The resulting 'valley-orbital-symmetry framework' provides a systematic guide for engineering correlated and topological quantum phases.
main_problem: To develop a general organizing principle for understanding the diverse emergent low-energy moiré Hamiltonians arising from twisted van der Waals heterostructures, moving beyond conventional single-orbital/K-valley paradigms.
main_result: The authors established a comprehensive 'valley-orbital-symmetry framework' that classifies emergent moiré physics based on parent material properties and symmetry constraints. This framework reveals multiple routes to correlated phases, including honeycomb, kagome, and multi-orbital flat bands.
method: The study combines fully relaxed first-principles calculations (DFT) with advanced analysis techniques like band unfolding, elementary band representation (EBR), and detailed symmetry group theory applied across hundreds of twisted bilayers.
model_or_system: The physical system is the moiré superlattice formed by twisting van der Waals bilayers. The theoretical framework aims to map the parent material's electronic structure ($\mathbf{k}_0, \mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{k}_0}$) onto an effective low-energy Hamiltonian defined by symmetry ($G_M$) and orbital content.
key_observables: Wannier characterization (W), band connectivity (C), topological classification (I), and the resulting $Q$-lattice structure are key diagnostics used to classify emergent models.
important_parameters: The analysis spans over 600 commensurate twisted bilayers across all 2D lattice classes, focusing on low-energy manifolds derived from parent band edges.
main_assumptions: The approach assumes that the physics can be systematically organized by mapping parent band edge properties and symmetry constraints to the emergent moiré Hamiltonian structure.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the design map connecting parent band edge properties to the resulting moiré Hamiltonians, while other figures detail specific flat-band manifolds realized in various lattice classes.
paper_structure: The paper introduces a general organizing map linking momentum location ($\mathbf{k}_0$), orbital character ($\mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{k}_0}$), and symmetry ($G_M$) to the resulting moiré Hamiltonian. It then systematically applies this framework across numerous material examples, demonstrating how different symmetries enforce specific types of correlated models (e.g., honeycomb vs. kagome).
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful theoretical dictionary for designing strongly correlated quantum materials by linking fundamental crystal symmetry and orbital physics directly to the required Hubbard model parameters.
